response.rationale: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma best fits the chronic unilateral subcutaneous spindle-cell proliferation with mature adipocytes infiltrating skeletal muscle and thickened collagen, without pleomorphism. Nodular fasciitis is less likely due to the 10-year course and lack of myxoid stroma.

rejected.why: Madelung's disease typically symmetric and cervical; unilateral nasal/cheek involvement and spindle-cell collagen changes are atypical.
Scleroderma lacks the adipocyte infiltration and spindle-cell proliferation described.
Same as R1; no specific support and symmetric distribution absent.
Nerve tissue tumor lacks specific neural features; spindle cells alone are nonspecific.
Sebaceous hyperplasia was the initial misinterpreted biopsy, not the final diagnosis.
